literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1 and L2) describe the same experiment: CRISPR insertion of a HiBiT epitope tag into the Alu exon of the endogenous IFNAR2-S isoform. IFNAR2-S is a naturally truncated, soluble isoform that arises from inclusion of an Alu-derived exon that introduces an early stop codon, eliminating the transmembrane domain. The resulting protein is secreted rather than membrane-anchored. This is functionally equivalent to a 'soluble ectodomain' construct, which the rules explicitly disqualify: 'The construct must be full-length and membrane-anchored.' Additionally, the Alu exon is not present in the canonical 515-aa IFNAR2 sequence (UniProt P48551), so no position in canonical numbering can be derived. L1 and L2 are also redundant (same quote, same experiment — one PMC, one preprint DOI). No other ledger lines exist. Zero sites qualify.
